storyboard.claim: Gray both causes the sting and rushes in to soothe it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray leaning in to hand a wincing Avery an ice pack for pain he just caused.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the vending-machine hornet metaphor into Gray's own move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the SAME person doing both halves of the loop, not two separate forces.

storyboard.claim: Avery is constantly reading Gray's face to guess what happens next.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery studying Gray's expression, tense and watchful.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the cost of beat 80's unpredictability: constant vigilance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the hypervigilance on her face and posture, not just the idea of it.

storyboard.claim: The reward hits harder because she never knows which outcome is coming.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The book's slot machine icon, standing in for the candy-bar-or-hornet gamble.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Literalizes 'candy bar or a hornet day' as the gamble it is.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly restates the vending/slot analogy already spoken.

storyboard.claim: The relief after terror is the most powerful high there is.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A jolt/zap icon over Avery, her nervous system firing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains WHY beat 82's spike is so strong: proportionate to prior fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the abstract 'dopamine spike' a felt physical jolt.

storyboard.claim: Gray is deliberately engineering a trauma bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray as the controlling figure, Avery the one being moved.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the mechanism the last few beats have been building.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer icon makes his calculation visible instead of just stated.

storyboard.claim: Avery becomes addicted to the relief only Gray can give from terror he causes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery reaching toward Gray, drawn in despite the danger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the trauma-bond mechanism named in beat 84.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reach gesture shows compulsion, not choice.

storyboard.claim: A normal gambler, or someone facing a hornet-shooting machine, can simply leave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure walking out an open door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the flaw in the analogy: real exits exist outside Avery's situation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the contrast the next beats use against Avery, who can't leave.

storyboard.claim: Gray works to remove every exit so Avery can't just walk away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery bound in place, Gray controlling the space around her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly answers beat 86's open door: Gray closes it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains make 'no exit' a visible fact, not just a phrase.

storyboard.claim: Lilyale itself is already a physical quarantine, before Gray adds anything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery small against the looming facility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms out from Gray's tactics to the building that houses them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes scale: the institution itself, not yet the psychological layer.

storyboard.claim: Black metal gates, armed guards, and keypad doors define Lilyale as a literal fortress.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery at a locked, keypad-coded door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives beat 88's 'quarantine' its concrete detail.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the security specific: keypad + staff card, not a vague prison.

storyboard.claim: The real trap isn't the concrete walls — it's entirely psychological.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum weighing physical walls against the far heavier psychological cage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns beat 89's literal fortress into the video's real claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the pivot from physical to psychological measurable, not just asserted.

storyboard.claim: Gray methodically isolates Avery from her few remaining connections.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray narrowing Avery's path away from other people.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows HOW the psychological cage from beat 90 gets built.
storyboard.addedInformation: Funnel shape makes the narrowing-over-time visible in one image.

callout.text: GRAY CUTS HER OFF FROM THEO

storyboard.claim: When Avery starts connecting with Theo, Gray steps in to warn her off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray stepping between Avery and Theo with a possessive arm, Avery looking back at Theo being blocked.
storyboard.onScreenText: GRAY CUTS HER OFF FROM THEO
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the funnel a first named target: Theo.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific connection being cut, not isolation in the abstract.

storyboard.claim: The other inmates, Saoon and Sam, make the environment itself hostile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fragile, hollow Saoon beside stocky, sneering Sam — two very different dangers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the environment doing isolation's other half, beyond Gray's own moves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Distinguishes two different threats (grief-shattered vs. aggressive) instead of one blob.

storyboard.claim: The hostile environment naturally pushes Avery away from the general population.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery flinching away from the common area full of threatening inmates — the environment itself is the force.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up beat 93: the environment does half of Gray's isolation work.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly restates the sentence just spoken.

storyboard.claim: Avery retreats to the dusty, abandoned library as her safe space.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery entering the mold-smelling, disused library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers 'where does Avery go' from beat 94.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the retreat in a specific place, not a vague 'away'.

storyboard.claim: Avery herself frames the library as where she'll finally be alone and safe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery sitting alone among the library shelves.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives beat 95's retreat her own words for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her own quote shows this is a CHOICE she believes is good for her.

storyboard.claim: Unlike a kidnapping, Macca builds the trap from small, reasonable-seeming decisions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery weighing a small, ordinary choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explicitly rejects the 'locked in a basement' cliché as the wrong picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Keeps the visual ordinary and small, matching the book's actual mechanism.

storyboard.claim: Avery chooses to avoid the loud common areas and hide in the library.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery slipping away toward the library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First concrete example of beat 97's micro decisions.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates beat 95/96's retreat with the word 'chooses' emphasized.

storyboard.claim: Avery actively participates in her own isolation, believing she's building a sanctuary.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery arranging the library space around her, book in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows her actively shaping the space beat 98 just chose.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her calm, purposeful action shows she believes this helps her — the irony is in what comes next.

storyboard.claim: Gray already treats the library as his own personal hunting blind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray waiting quietly among the shelves, watching for her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the sanctuary from beat 99 was already compromised.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Gray was there first, waiting — the sanctuary was never truly hers.

storyboard.claim: Gray seamlessly infiltrates the one space Avery thought was safe from him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray entering the library as Avery notices, caught off guard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the reveal from beat 100: he doesn't just wait, he moves in.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her surprise shows the safe space failing in real time.

storyboard.claim: Real-world parallel: slowly dropping a friend group because a new partner preferred just the two of you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure walking away from a group, alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls the book's pattern into a relatable real-world example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the abstract isolation mechanism in an experience many viewers recognize.

storyboard.claim: Adapting to keep the peace feels like romance at first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure quietly adjusting their own behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the real-world parallel: why the small changes feel good, not bad.
storyboard.addedInformation: Keeps the figure calm and unbothered — the danger isn't visible from inside it yet.

storyboard.claim: What feels like caring is actually the slow building of a wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure bound in place, the wall closing around them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what beat 103's 'romance' feeling actually is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains make the wall's real function — restriction — visible.

storyboard.claim: Because the victim makes these decisions themselves, they're blind to the partner shutting the door behind them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure walks forward unaware while behind them Gray is closing and locking the door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the real-world parallel with its final image: the door closes unseen.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the blindness itself: the figure isn't looking back at the door.

storyboard.claim: By retreating from the asylum's obvious threats, Avery walks into Gray's personalized cage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery moving away from screaming inmates and guards, straight toward Gray.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns from the real-world parallel to close the book's own isolation arc.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the whole isolation sequence (93-106) into one image: away from noise, into Gray.

storyboard.claim: Isolated and cut off, Avery's dopamine system now depends entirely on Gray's unpredictable rewards.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from isolation to dependence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the isolation arc's payoff as cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the causal chain explicit: isolation is the mechanism that produces the dependence.

storyboard.claim: Avery's emotional vault is now unlocked, opening the book's most uncomfortable material.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery holding a key, the vault open.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the dependence beat 107 set up, and pivots toward what's next.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals a tonal turn — what follows will be harder material.

storyboard.claim: The real test of this rewiring does NOT happen in a conversation about feelings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray standing silently, not talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the expected venue (talk) to set up the physiological one that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck-through text makes the rejection explicit rather than staging a fake conversation.

storyboard.claim: Avery's logical mind screams danger, but her body tells a completely different story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery with her hand on her racing heart — her terrified face contradicts her body pulling toward Gray.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the physiological test beat 109 promised instead of a conversation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the mind/body split on one body at once: worried face, racing heart.

storyboard.claim: The video is moving into the book's most boundary-pushing scenes: the library and the morgue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray together in the library, tension building.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Signals a shift into the specific scenes the physiological claim will illustrate.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly a signpost for what's coming.

storyboard.claim: In the library scene, Gray uses a bloodied weapon as a tool for stimulation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray and Avery in close, tense proximity in the library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the first of the two boundary-pushing scenes flagged in beat 111.
storyboard.addedInformation: Keeps the depiction restrained — proximity and tension, not graphic detail.

storyboard.claim: Gray tells her, 'I'm your god now, little killer, and I'm your devil too.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray's true, dark self surfacing behind his usual face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the scene from beat 112 its defining line of dialogue.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shadow self makes visible what the quote states outright: this is who he really is.

storyboard.claim: Gray is simultaneously the threat of lethal violence and the source of intense pleasure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single jolt hitting Avery, threat and pleasure arriving together.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the hornet-and-ice-pack pattern from beat 80, now literal.
storyboard.addedInformation: One jolt for both halves shows they are simultaneous, not sequential.

storyboard.claim: Avery's conscious mind is terrified — panicking about the guards, knowing exactly what Gray is.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery tense, afraid, alert to being caught.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the 'conscious mind' half of the split from beat 114.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names her clear-eyed knowledge of the danger, not confusion.

storyboard.claim: Even knowing the bleed could kill her, Avery's body responds with overwhelming physical pleasure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery's racing heart, her body's response at odds with her fear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the 'body' half of the split beat 115 set up on the mind side.
storyboard.addedInformation: Repeats the heart from beat 110 to show the same body now overruling the mind.

storyboard.claim: The text's own words: 'my heart races as I feel myself rushing towards the edge.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery caught in the moment the quote describes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives beat 116's claim the book's own quoted language.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses Avery's own words rather than the narrators paraphrasing her.

storyboard.claim: As a society, we desperately want arousal and consent to be the exact same thing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman figure trying to force two separate concepts into one neat box — the societal wish that consent and arousal always align.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms out from Avery's own scene to the reader's discomfort with it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shifts the claim from 'what happened to Avery' to 'what we expect from bodies in general'.

storyboard.claim: We want it simple: a single morally clean package where consent and arousal always match.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The neat package cracking open — biology refusing to fit inside the moral framework.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the wish beat 118 named, setting up its collapse in the next chunk.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates the desire for simplicity just spoken, sets up the reveal that follows.
